trials.name: footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: Keep the starting body. Score each brick type by pooling learned features over its own footprint (max, min and mean), then pass them through a small per-type layer. Min-pooling acts like 'every footprint cell is missing at the landing layer', and max-pooling can track the highest point under the footprint, which sets the landing layer. Compute is about 1.16x the starting network. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.35.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
PROJ = 32
HID = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        T = spec.n_types
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_hidden = nn.Conv2d(T * 3 * PROJ, T * HID, 1, groups=T)
        self.type_out = nn.Conv2d(T * HID, T, 1, groups=T)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        p = self.proj(f)
        pooled = []
        for (dy, dx) in self.footprints:
            q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            pooled += [mx, mn, av]
        h = torch.cat(pooled, dim=1)
        place = self.type_out(F.relu(self.type_hidden(h))).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: 3D voxel encoder
trials.hypothesis: Treat layers as a spatial axis. Two 3x3x3 Conv3d layers (width 16) read each voxel's build, target, missing and extra values plus a z coordinate. Learned projections of column heights and time are added in. The voxel features are then flattened over z into a 1x1 2D layer and the starting heads. One set of weights covers every layer, so 'missing here, filled below' is learned once rather than once per layer. Compute is about 1x. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.35.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

VW = 16
WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = spec.Z
        self.Z = Z
        self.c1 = nn.Conv3d(5, VW, 3, padding=1)
        self.g1 = nn.Conv2d(3, VW, 1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv3d(VW, VW, 3, padding=1)
        self.flat = nn.Conv2d(VW * Z, WIDTH, 1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        if Z > 1:
            zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z)
        else:
            zc = torch.zeros(1)
        self.register_buffer('zc', zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1))

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        zc = self.zc.expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        vox = torch.cat([vox, zc], dim=1)
        h = self.c1(vox) + self.g1(obs[:, 4 * Z:]).unsqueeze(2)
        h = F.relu(h)
        h = F.relu(self.c2(h))
        h = h.reshape(B, VW * Z, Y, X)
        f = F.relu(self.flat(h))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        for m in self.modules():
            if isinstance(m, (nn.Conv2d, nn.Linear)):
                nn.init.orthogonal_(m.weight, gain=math.sqrt(2.0))
                nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.place_head.weight, gain=0.01)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.done_head.weight, gain=0.01)
        nn.init.orthogonal_(self.value_head.weight, gain=1.0)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
K = 12
HID = 12


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.T = spec.n_types
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        Z, T = self.Z, self.T
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.layer_proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, Z * K, 1)
        self.vox_proj = nn.Conv3d(9, K, 1)
        self.type_hidden = nn.Conv3d(T * 3 * K, T * HID, 1, groups=T)
        self.type_out = nn.Conv3d(T * HID, 2 * T, 1, groups=T)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.type_out.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.type_out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        if Z > 1:
            zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z)
        else:
            zc = torch.zeros(1)
        self.register_buffer('zc', zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1))

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z, T = self.Z, self.T
        f = self.body(obs)
        build = obs[:, 0:Z]
        target = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        missing = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        extra = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        build_below = F.pad(build, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0), value=1.0)[:, :Z]
        missing_below = F.pad(missing, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0), value=0.0)[:, :Z]
        height = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        theight = obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        zc = self.zc.expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        vox = torch.stack([build, target, missing, extra, build_below, missing_below], dim=1)
        vox = torch.cat([vox, height, theight, zc], dim=1)
        p = F.relu(self.layer_proj(f).reshape(B, K, Z, Y, X) + self.vox_proj(vox))
        pooled = []
        for (dy, dx) in self.footprints:
            q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool3d(q, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool3d(-q, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool3d(q, (1, dy, dx), stride=1)
            pooled += [mx, mn, av]
        h = torch.cat(pooled, dim=1)
        o = self.type_out(F.relu(self.type_hidden(h))).reshape(B, T, 2, Z, Y, X)
        w = torch.softmax(o[:, :, 1], dim=2)
        place = (w * o[:, :, 0]).sum(2).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        self.skip = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, SKIPH, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(SKIPH, PROJ, 1))
        self.type_hidden = nn.Conv2d(T * 3 * PROJ, T * HID, 1, groups=T)
        self.type_out = nn.Conv2d(T * HID, T, 1, groups=T)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.type_out.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.type_out.bias)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        p = F.relu(self.proj(f) + self.skip(obs))
        pooled = []
        for (dy, dx) in self.footprints:
            q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            pooled += [mx, mn, av]
        h = torch.cat(pooled, dim=1)
        place = self.type_out(F.relu(self.type_hidden(h))).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: Add GroupNorm (8 groups) after each body convolution in r2c1. Seeds that end at 0.16 to 0.32 suggest the early optimisation is unstable. Normalised activations keep feature scales steady as the build fills in and reduce dead ReLUs, which should make good runs more consistent. The network is otherwise unchanged and costs almost nothing extra. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.50, or if either seed is below 0.33.

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting network scored 0.541, 0.160, 0.160 and 0.518 over 4 seeds, so seed luck alone moves the score by about 0.38. A gain should count only if it is large or repeats across seeds. The budget is tiny: 128 PPO updates. So candidates should stay near the starting network's compute, because a bigger network gets fewer training steps. Exact building needs two things. First, a brick's landing layer is the highest filled cell anywhere under its footprint. Second, every cell it fills must be missing from the build at that same layer. The starting network scores a 2x2 brick from its anchor cell's features alone, and it mixes all layers into one input stack. This round tests three ideas: (1) a placement head that pools features over each brick's footprint; (2) a 3D convolution that treats layers as a spatial axis; (3) standard PPO initialisation (orthogonal weights, near-zero policy outputs), aimed at the seed-to-seed swings.
analyses.2: Dev success looks bimodal. Four seeds of the starting network gave 0.54, 0.16, 0.16 and 0.52. Both seeds of r1c2 (3D convs) and r1c3 (orthogonal init) stalled near 0.16. My guess is that 0.16 is a stable trap: the agent may build only with 1x1 bricks, which only works on designs without overhangs. I haven't tested this. The footprint-pooled head (r1c1) is the only candidate whose seeds both avoided that trap (0.35 and 0.39). Its mean is close to the baseline's 0.345, but it was steadier between seeds, and it trained on only 99k steps. This suggests that giving the head explicit features for each brick type and footprint helps the agent find out when bigger bricks fit. Next tests: (1) feed raw input features into the footprint pooling through a learned 1x1 layer; (2) a deeper, narrower body at about the same compute; (3) score each layer separately, with a learned guess of which layer the brick lands on (new idea). If all of these fall back to 0.16, the pooled head is not what helps.
analyses.3: Only r2c1 (footprint-pooled head plus raw 1x1 skip) beats the start: 0.519 mean, but its seeds were 0.71 and 0.32, so the true gain is uncertain. r1c1 (pooled head without the skip) at 0.368 is about the same as the start. That points to sharp per-cell signals at the head as the useful ingredient. Three ideas lost to the start: the 3D voxel encoder (0.17), orthogonal init (0.16, both seeds collapsed) and the per-layer landing gate (0.22). The deeper, narrower body (0.35) did not help either. Repeated 0.1602 scores suggest a shared failure mode, probably a poor DONE decision or no handling of overhangs. All three proposals keep r2c1 as the base and change one thing each: (1) sharp skip features feed the DONE and value heads, since DONE is right only when nothing is missing; (2) a cheaper body, so the run gets the full 131k steps; (3) board-wide context is broadcast into the per-cell head, for ordering decisions.
analyses.4: The best evidence so far is that the head should score each brick by pooling over its own footprint and should receive sharp per-cell features. Adding a raw 1x1 skip gave the best result: r2c1 at 0.519 and r3c1 at 0.501. Both are above r1c1 (0.368) and the start (0.345), but each seed pair differs by about 0.4, so the gain is not certain. Giving anchors more reach made things worse: a deeper body (r2c2, 0.349) and adding a board-wide context vector to every cell (r3c3, 0.321) both scored lower. The 3D and per-layer designs (r1c2, r2c3) and orthogonal small-gain initialisation (r1c3) failed. A narrower body with more training steps (r3c2, 0.393) did not help either, although that difference is within seed noise. For this last round I refine r2c1 with one change each: a richer per-cell skip, more capacity in the per-type scorer, and normalisation in the body to make seeds less likely to fail.
